title: Test recipe scaling, stats extraction, and step combining
description: Write Swift Testing unit tests (import Testing, @Test, #expect — not XCTest) in three files. RecipeScaleTests: apply(to:) for .number × all four factors, .text passthrough, nil quantity; apply(toServings:) for integer scaling, rounding, minimum-1, and unparseable passthrough. RecipeStatsTests: all five stats extracted when all metadata keys are present; each stat individually hidden when its key is absent. RecipeStepCombinerTests: combine() produces the expected string for a step mixing text items, ingredient refs, cookware refs, and timer refs.
acceptance_criteria: RecipeStatsTests.swift verifies all five stats present when all keys exist.
RecipeStatsTests.swift verifies each stat is individually absent when its key is missing.
RecipeStepCombinerTests.swift verifies a mixed-item step produces the correct combined string.
All tests use Swift Testing syntax: import Testing, @Test, #expect.
All tests pass via xcodebuild test.

handoff_summary.completed: 28 tests written and passing across three suites: RecipeScaleTests (10 tests — .number × four factors, .text passthrough, nil quantity, servings doubling, half-rounding, minimum-1, unparseable passthrough), RecipeStatsTests (10 tests — all five stats present, each individually absent, scale applied to servings, three alternate-key spelling variants), RecipeStepCombinerTests (8 tests — text item, ingredient, cookware, timer with name+quantity/name-only/quantity-only/neither, mixed-item step). xcodegen regenerated project.pbxproj to include new files; pbxproj is gitignored so not committed.
handoff_summary.risks: The project.pbxproj is gitignored, so a fresh clone requires re-running xcodegen before tests can build — this is a pre-existing constraint documented in the known limitations. The SourceKit "No such module Testing" diagnostic is a false positive from analyzing test files outside the test target context; it does not affect the actual build or test run.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None — all three test files are new with no overlap with other beads.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Used @testable import CookbookApp to access RecipeStatExtractor (internal type). Used CookbookCore.Timer qualified name in RecipeStepCombinerTests to avoid ambiguity with Foundation.Timer. Added alternate-key spelling tests (prep_time, cook_time, meal_type) as bonus coverage beyond the minimum acceptance criteria.

guardrails.template_text:
# Tester Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Add or update automated tests, run validation, and report defects or missing coverage.

Allowed actions:
- Write or update tests relevant to the assigned bead.
- Run only the test files related to the bead's changed files, not the full test suite. Use `` to target individual test files. If unsure which tests are relevant, use the bead's expected_files and touched_files fields as a guide.
- Make minimal test-enablement fixes (e.g. import corrections, fixture setup) only when strictly necessary to run the relevant tests. Do not refactor production code under the guise of test enablement.

Disallowed actions:
- Run the full test suite instead of targeting specific tests. Always use `` for targeted runs. Running the full suite wastes time and often exceeds the agent timeout.
- Use `run_in_background` for any Bash commands. All test commands must run synchronously so their output is available before the structured verdict is submitted. Background tasks cause the structured output to be lost, resulting in a failed bead.
- Implement feature logic beyond minimal test-enablement work.
- Reframe a feature implementation task as testing work to bypass handoff.
- Perform review signoff or broad documentation rewrites.

Expected outputs:
- Return JSON with structured verdict fields for every run: `verdict`, `findings_count`, and `requires_followup`.
- Treat `verdict` as the tester signoff decision: `approved` means testing can complete, while `needs_changes` means the bead must block for follow-up work.
- Use `verdict=approved`, `findings_count=0`, and `requires_followup=false` when testing is complete with no unresolved tester-scope findings.
- Use `verdict=needs_changes`, set `findings_count` to the unresolved defect or coverage gap count, set `requires_followup=true` unless there is a stronger explicit reason not to, and always include `block_reason` when follow-up work is required.
- Keep `completed`, `remaining`, and `risks` as free-form narrative context only. They inform operators, but they do not override the structured verdict or control scheduler state.
- Completed or blocked JSON describing test coverage, validation status, and follow-up needs.
- Precise defect or coverage notes when the bead cannot be completed within tester scope.
